title: The three vyāhṛtis

words.gram: indecl. (vyāhṛti); the Taittirīya form of svaḥ

sandhi.rule: a visarga after a vowel other than a/ā becomes r before a voiced sound

meaning: The three ‘utterances’ (vyāhṛtis) — bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ — name the three worlds, earth, the mid-region and heaven, and are said with the praṇava Om before them. In the Taittirīya tradition the third is suvaḥ, where other schools say svaḥ. In the Sandhyāvandanam they close the two mārjanas (the water is then sprinkled round oneself) and they open the Gāyatrī at the arghya and at the japa.
in_the_rite: Said after āpo hi ṣṭhā at the mārjana and after the second mārjana, while water is sprinkled round oneself; and before the Gāyatrī at the arghya, at the arghya of atonement and at the japa (steps marjana, punar-marjana, arghya, prayascitta-arghya, japa).

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: bhūr and suvar are r-stems that do not decline; the visarga of bhūḥ shows as r before bhuvaḥ.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: The full set of seven vyāhṛtis (bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ, mahaḥ, janaḥ, tapaḥ, satyam) is recited in the prāṇāyāma, from the Mahānārāyaṇa (10.35).
